title: Air Power Not Air Forces with Tobias Switzer
gist: A CNAS podcast episode features Tobias Switzer discussing a new RAND report arguing that U.S. security force assistance to partner nations should prioritize generating effective, affordable combat airpower over replicating Western-style air force institutions, drawing on lessons from Iraq and Afghanistan.

insights.claim: Tobias Bernard Switzer's new RAND report, 'Air Power, Not Air Forces,' argues that U.S. security force assistance should prioritize generating effective combat airpower in partner nations rather than replicating Western-style air force institutions.
insights.speaker: Tobias Switzer
insights.so_what: A direct critique of decades of U.S. security-assistance doctrine, relevant to how defense-industrial and training contracts for partner-nation air forces might be restructured going forward.
insights.locator: his new RAND report, Air Power, Not Air Forces

insights.claim: The report draws lessons from U.S. efforts to build partner aviation capabilities in Iraq and Afghanistan, using those programs as case studies for what worked and what did not in security force assistance.
insights.speaker: Tobias Switzer
insights.so_what: Frames two of the largest post-9/11 security-assistance programs as cautionary case studies for how future partner-capacity investment should be designed.
insights.locator: the lessons drawn from U.S. efforts to build partner aviation capabilities

insights.claim: Switzer emphasizes affordable capabilities, sustainable support, and organizational approaches better suited to partner needs, rather than expensive, high-end Western equipment and institutional templates.
insights.speaker: Tobias Switzer
insights.so_what: Suggests a market opportunity for lower-cost, sustainment-friendly defense platforms and training packages over premium Western systems when selling into partner-nation air power programs.
